label: amplitude_probe
note: Pre-learning readout statistics at HEAD (7dd3bd6, Shiu absolute scale), 16 shared reference states, input_drive_mv=20.0 (the INPUT_GAIN used by commit 1386b35 which produced amendment A4 and pilot_v783_a4).

drive_sweep_real_arm._units: median sd over all 44 output units; zero throughout because >50% of units never leave v_rest

findings: At the committed INPUT_DRIVE_MV=0.06 every one of the 44 output units is constant at v_rest=-52mV in all three arms: the readout carries no game-state information at all.
Raising the drive 3300x (to 200 mV) does not fix it; >50% of output units never leave rest. This is the sparsity cause amendment A4 diagnosed, not a gain problem.
At the old INPUT_GAIN=20.0 the live-unit signal is ~1700x weaker than A4 recorded (0.041 vs 70.1) and only ~half the units vary, versus all of them in A4.
The arm ordering A4 recorded (real>shuffled>random) does not reproduce at HEAD: shuffled and random have swapped (real 0.0408 > random 0.0092 > shuffled 0.0067).

Consequence for fly-ky7.11: the amplitude control is implemented and verified, but no verdict can be drawn at HEAD, because the pre-learning amplitude ordering it exists to neutralise is itself absent.
